dosing.evidence: Psilocin 1 and 4 mg/kg ... was dissolved in saline (0.9% NaCl) acidified with 10 m l of glacial acetic acid. All injections were administered subcutaneously (s.c.) at a volume of 2 ml/kg. Rats were trained 4 days, 30 min after psilocin injection.

assays.assay_description: Active place avoidance on a rotating circular arena (82 cm diameter, 1 rpm). 4 acquisition sessions (days 1-4, psilocin 30 min before) + 1 drug-free session on day 5. Measures: total distance traveled, number of entrances into shock sector, maximum time avoided.

setup_restrain.evidence: rats freely moving on rotating arena; harness with LED only

food_restriction.evidence: Water and food were available ad libitum throughout the experiments (none in apparatus during testing).

water_restriction.evidence: Water and food were available ad libitum throughout the experiments (none in apparatus during testing).

time_to_assay.evidence: Rats were trained 4 days, 30 min after psilocin injection

sample_size.evidence: Eight animals were used in each group (24 rats in total).

outcomes.summary: Psilocin impaired acquisition of the Carousel maze at both 1 and 4 mg/kg, indicated by more entrances into the shock sector and lower maximum time avoided. The 4 mg/kg dose reduced locomotor activity in early sessions and blocked learning even in the drug-free day-5 session.
outcomes.evidence: Psilocin significantly impaired the acquisition of the Carousel maze at both doses (1 and 4 mg/kg). The higher dose of psilocin blocked the learning processes even in an additional session when the rats received only saline.

assays.assay_description: Spatial navigation in a circular pool (180 cm diameter, water 20 °C, 40 cm deep) with hidden platform in NE quadrant. Eight swims per session, max 60 s/trial. Two experiments: (1) reinforced retrieval — 4 drug-free acquisition days, Day 5 test under psilocin (1 or 4 mg/kg, 30 min pre), drug-free re-acquisition 5 days later; (2) consolidation — Day 1 16-trial training followed by post-training psilocin injection, Day 2 drug-free re-test. Measure: escape latency.

application_type.evidence: psilocin was applied s.c. (1 or 4 mg/kg) 30 min prior to testing

setup_restrain.evidence: Rats were released facing the wall ... freely swimming

food_restriction.evidence: Water and food were available ad libitum throughout the experiments (none in apparatus during testing).

water_restriction.evidence: Water and food were available ad libitum throughout the experiments (none in apparatus during testing).

time_to_assay.evidence: psilocin was applied s.c. (1 or 4 mg/kg) 30 min prior to testing (retrieval); psilocin was injected immediately after the last swim (consolidation), tested on subsequent day

sample_size.evidence: Eight animals were used in each group (24 rats in total) [for retrieval]; Eight animals were used in each group (24 rats in total) [for consolidation].

outcomes.summary: Psilocin 4 mg/kg disrupted reinforced retrieval (increased escape latency on Day 5), and the impairment persisted in a drug-free re-acquisition 5 days later; 1 mg/kg had no significant effect. Neither dose injected post-training affected memory consolidation tested on Day 2.
outcomes.evidence: The dose of 4 mg/kg disrupted reinforced retrieval in the MWM. However, the application of a lower dose was without any significant effect. Finally, neither the low nor high dose of psilocin injected post-training caused a deficit in memory consolidation in the MWM.

B1_num_measures.evidence: we recorded the latency to find the platform as a measure of spatial memory

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Repeated measures across sessions/days, but no within-session time-course analysis

B6_cognitive.evidence: spatial memory ... allocentric spatial memory ... acquisition, consolidation, and retrieval

B7_automated_classification.evidence: The escape latency was recorded by the experimenter using a stopwatch

E1_environment_type.evidence: blue-painted metallic circular tank (180 cm in diameter, 50 cm high) filled with water

E2_shelter.evidence: open water tank; submerged platform is the goal, not a refuge

D1_continuity.evidence: four acquisition sessions ... On Day 5 ... Five days later ... On the subsequent day (Day 2)

D2_session_duration.evidence: One daily session consisted of eight swims; if the rat failed to find the platform in 60 s, the trial was stopped, plus 10 s on platform — eight trials yields a session of roughly 15–60 min.

D3_recording_days.evidence: Retrieval experiment: 4 acquisition days + Day 5 test + Day 10 drug-free re-test = 6 recording days. Consolidation experiment: Day 1 + Day 2 = 2 days.

D4_baseline.evidence: Animals from all groups were pre-trained in the reference memory version of the MWM for 4 days without drug injections

D5_followup.evidence: Five days later, drug-free animals underwent another re-acquisition; consolidation tested 24 h after dosing

judge_notes: Two assays retained: Carousel maze and Morris water maze. MWM reinforced-retrieval and post-training consolidation experiments collapsed into ONE MWM assay per rubric (same apparatus, same paradigm, different drug timing).

Psilocin dosing schedule scored 'repeated' for Carousel maze (4 daily doses) but kept single dosing entry at study level; chose 'repeated' as the dominant regimen since Carousel used 4 daily doses and MWM used 1 dose.
B2 (temporal dynamics) scored 0 for both assays: repeated-measures ANOVA across sessions/days is between-session, not within-session minute-by-minute analysis.

MWM D2 scored 1 (15–60 min) based on the explicit 8 swims × up to 60 s + 10 s platform structure, giving session durations within that bin; medium confidence as exact session length not stated as a single number.
Carousel D2 scored 0 with low confidence — no explicit per-session duration stated.
Session 5 of Carousel maze is a drug-free re-test 24 h after last dose, qualifying for D5 follow-up.
MWM time_to_assay marked 'multiple' because reinforced retrieval (30 min post-dose) and consolidation (24 h post-dose) timepoints are merged into one assay entry.
